title: English Theory Atlas
description: A structured map from basic grammar to the sound, meaning, social and historical systems that make English a real living language.

domains.name: Grammar Architecture
domains.description: How English builds phrases, clauses and viewpoints.

topics.name: Sentence spine & word order
topics.note: Subject, verb, objects, complements and why position carries meaning.

topics.name: Word classes & phrase structure
topics.note: Nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, determiners, prepositions and how they form phrases.

topics.name: Nouns, countability & number
topics.note: How English packages things as countable, uncountable, singular, plural and collective.

topics.name: Articles & determiners
topics.note: a/an, the, zero article, this/that, some/any and shared knowledge.

topics.name: Pronouns & reference
topics.note: Personal, reflexive, demonstrative and indefinite reference across conversation.

topics.name: Tense & aspect
topics.note: Present, past, perfect and progressive as viewpoint systems — not only time labels.

topics.name: Future meanings
topics.note: will, be going to, present continuous, present simple and modal ways to frame the future.

topics.name: Modality
topics.note: Ability, obligation, permission, advice, probability and speaker attitude.

topics.name: Questions & negation
topics.note: Auxiliary movement, do-support, question types, tags and negative scope.

topics.name: Comparison & degree
topics.note: Comparatives, superlatives, intensifiers, downtoners and scalar meaning.

topics.name: Relative & noun clauses
topics.note: Embed descriptions and entire ideas inside larger sentences.

topics.name: Conditionals
topics.note: Real, hypothetical, counterfactual and mixed realities beyond 0/1/2/3 formulas.

topics.name: Passive voice
topics.note: Move attention from agent to event, result or affected entity.

topics.name: Reported speech
topics.note: Represent another voice with shifts in tense, deixis and stance.

topics.name: Gerunds, infinitives & participles
topics.note: Non-finite verb forms and the different ways English packages actions.

topics.name: Emphasis, inversion & advanced syntax
topics.note: Clefts, fronting, inversion, ellipsis and marked word order for focus and style.

domains.name: Sound & Pronunciation
domains.description: How spoken English is physically produced and compressed in real time.

topics.name: IPA & phonemes
topics.note: Map English vowel and consonant contrasts so spelling stops controlling pronunciation.

topics.name: Syllables & word stress
topics.note: Primary/secondary stress, stress shifts and why wrong stress blocks recognition.

topics.name: Schwa & weak vowels
topics.note: The central reduced vowel that powers natural English rhythm.

topics.name: Sentence stress
topics.note: Prominence marks content, contrast and new information.

topics.name: Connected speech
topics.note: Linking, assimilation, elision and resyllabification across word boundaries.

topics.name: Weak forms & reductions
topics.note: Why function words shrink and common sequences compress in fluent speech.

topics.name: Rhythm
topics.note: Stress-timed tendency, timing groups and how unstressed material is squeezed.

topics.name: Intonation
topics.note: Pitch movement signals completeness, attitude, contrast, politeness and involvement.

topics.name: Accent flexibility
topics.note: Build perception across native and international accents without copying one identity blindly.

domains.name: Vocabulary & Meaning
domains.description: Why knowing a word means far more than knowing its translation.

topics.name: High-frequency vocabulary
topics.note: Prioritize words with broad conversational usefulness and deep mastery.

topics.name: Chunks & formulaic language
topics.note: Store ready-made sequences by communicative function for faster retrieval.

topics.name: Collocation
topics.note: Natural word partnerships such as make sense, heavy rain and deeply concerned.

topics.name: Word families & morphology
topics.note: Roots, prefixes, suffixes, derivation and conversion between word classes.

topics.name: Phrasal verbs & particles
topics.note: Understand particle imagery rather than memorizing thousands of disconnected definitions.

topics.name: Polysemy & semantic networks
topics.note: Connect multiple senses of one word around a core conceptual meaning.

topics.name: Idioms & metaphor
topics.note: Use conventional figurative language selectively and understand conceptual metaphors.

topics.name: Register & connotation
topics.note: Choose words by relationship, context, emotional coloring and level of formality.

domains.name: Discourse & Pragmatics
domains.description: The hidden social system behind natural conversation.

topics.name: Speech acts
topics.note: Requests, offers, invitations, apologies, refusals and promises as social actions.

topics.name: Turn-taking
topics.note: Enter, hold, yield and reclaim the conversational floor naturally.

topics.name: Conversation repair
topics.note: Clarify, check understanding, reformulate and recover from mishearing.

topics.name: Discourse markers
topics.note: well, actually, anyway, so, I mean and other navigation signals.

topics.name: Cohesion & coherence
topics.note: Make ideas connect through reference, lexical chains, logical relations and information flow.

topics.name: Information structure
topics.note: Old/new information, topic/focus and how stress and word order guide attention.

topics.name: Politeness & softening
topics.note: Manage directness, social distance and face using modal, lexical and intonational choices.

topics.name: Implicature & indirect meaning
topics.note: Understand what is meant beyond what is literally said.

topics.name: Hedging, stance & nuance
topics.note: Signal certainty, evidence, evaluation and commitment without sounding absolute.

domains.name: Fluency & Skill Systems
domains.description: Turn knowledge into automatic comprehension and expression.

topics.name: Listening bottom-up
topics.note: Decode sounds, word boundaries, reductions and grammatical cues.

topics.name: Listening top-down
topics.note: Use context, prediction and world knowledge without guessing blindly.

topics.name: Shadowing & imitation
topics.note: Synchronize perception and speech to train rhythm, linking and automatic chunks.

topics.name: Spontaneous speaking
topics.note: Plan meaning in small units, buy time naturally and finish thoughts before self-editing.

topics.name: Paraphrase & circumlocution
topics.note: Keep communicating when the exact word is unavailable.

topics.name: Storytelling & long turns
topics.note: Organize setup, sequence, detail, evaluation and conclusion for sustained speech.

topics.name: Authentic input mining
topics.note: Turn podcasts, videos and conversations into reusable chunks and pronunciation models.

topics.name: English inner voice
topics.note: Move routine planning, self-talk, reactions and recall into English to reduce translation dependence.

domains.name: Semantics & Cognition
domains.description: How English packages experience into meanings, categories and viewpoints.

topics.name: Lexical semantics
topics.note: Meaning is a network of senses, contrasts and usage patterns — not a one-to-one translation.

topics.name: Compositional meaning
topics.note: How word meanings, syntax and context combine to produce the meaning of a whole utterance.

topics.name: Event structure
topics.note: How verbs frame actions, states, changes, causes, endpoints and participants.

topics.name: Deixis
topics.note: I/you, here/there, this/that, now/then depend on the speaker's viewpoint and situation.

topics.name: Definiteness & givenness
topics.note: Why English marks whether a referent is identifiable, new, shared or already active in discourse.

topics.name: Prototype & categorization
topics.note: Many categories have central and peripheral members rather than perfect dictionary boundaries.

topics.name: Conceptual metaphor
topics.note: Abstract English often grows from embodied patterns: time as space, arguments as movement, states as containers.

topics.name: Inference & enrichment
topics.note: Listeners routinely build intended meaning from context beyond the literal semantic content.

domains.name: English in Society & History
domains.description: Why modern English looks, sounds and changes the way it does across communities.

topics.name: Germanic core & borrowed layers
topics.note: English has a Germanic grammatical core plus major Norse, French, Latin and global lexical layers.

topics.name: Spelling vs sound history
topics.note: Historical sound changes and conservative spelling help explain why written and spoken English diverge.

topics.name: Dialect vs accent
topics.note: Accent concerns pronunciation; dialect can also differ in vocabulary and grammar. Variation is systematic, not broken English.

topics.name: World Englishes
topics.note: English is used globally with multiple legitimate norms, identities and communicative settings.

topics.name: Register, style & identity
topics.note: Speakers shift language by audience, purpose, community and the identity they want to project.

topics.name: Descriptive vs prescriptive grammar
topics.note: Separate how people actually use English from style rules recommended for particular contexts.

topics.name: Language change
topics.note: Pronunciation, grammar, vocabulary and meanings constantly evolve through repeated community use.

topics.name: Corpus thinking & frequency
topics.note: Judge naturalness with patterns across real usage, not intuition or isolated examples alone.

topics.name: Etymology without mythology
topics.note: Word history can explain development but does not dictate what a word must mean today.

topics.name: Intelligibility over imitation
topics.note: The goal is clear, flexible, socially appropriate English — not erasing your identity to copy one native accent.
